row.description: 3GPP PLMN display notation uses a three-digit Mobile Country Code and a two- or three-digit Mobile Network Code separated by a literal hyphen, as in 310-260. A wrong generalization would remove the hyphen because database forms often concatenate MCC and MNC, thereby accepting an unformatted identifier where this presentation convention requires the separator.

neighbors.relationship: A subscriber number may be served by a PLMN but does not encode MCC-MNC in this hyphenated form.
An IMSI begins with MCC and MNC but continues with a subscriber identity and is not written as a standalone PLMN code.

row.description: RFC 3261 SIP URI syntax permits a repeated semicolon-prefixed URI-parameter section after the host, for example transport and user parameters. A wrong generalization would model only one parameter because examples often show a single suffix, rejecting valid URIs with multiple parameter sections.

neighbors.relationship: A tel URI identifies a telephone number and uses different parameter rules from a SIP URI.
A Contact header may contain a SIP URI but additionally has header-level display-name and parameter syntax.

row.description: ITU-T E.164 international-number notation uses a leading plus sign followed by up to 15 digits. Samples from one national numbering plan can appear to have a fixed width, but E.164 is variable-width across country codes and national significant numbers. A wrong generalization would hard-code the apparent sample length, such as 11 digits, and reject valid shorter or longer international numbers.

neighbors.relationship: A national significant number is interpreted within a numbering plan and normally omits the E.164 plus form.
An IMSI is a mobile subscriber identity that can begin with country and network codes but is not an E.164 dialable number.
